Row.Text: The British captain leans down before the monument to lost sailors – sea and storm take who they can. But British fortunes also come from these waters – the sea gives both life and death. As the captain looks up at the horizon, a brief image appears before his eyes: a wooden wall. A line of ships. A future where others may rule their lands, but Britannia will rule the waves.
The roads on which British merchants will travel.
An engineering problem for British minds.

The idea of a secular, specialized knowledge is new to Britain, but it shows promise: young minds trained not to follow religious teachings, but to the workings of the world and society. New reformers imagine a system that addresses national priorities, whereas philosophers and scientists imagine knowledge without direction or limits. There are only so many seats in only so many classrooms.
Education should have direct, practical application to the national interest.
Education should follow intellectual paths, even if they are not immediately profitable.
